bull_bear.body:
- Concentration risk to Kalyani Group dividends — Main source of income is dividends from Kalyani Group Companies; any operational or financial distress in those investee companies could materially reduce dividend inflows.
- Securities market fluctuation and devaluation of investments — Fluctuations in the securities market and global economic scenario may pose a risk of devaluation of the Company's investment portfolio.
- Credit risk on loans and interest — Non-recovery of principal amounts lent and interest thereon could impair asset quality and income.
- Regulatory risk as a Core Investment Company — The Company operates as a Non-Deposit taking Core Investment Company under RBI Directions; any change in regulatory classification or non-compliance could affect its operating framework.
- Macro-economic sensitivity of investment decisions — The Company evaluates opportunities based on macro-economic conditions; adverse macro shifts could constrain investment returns and strategic deployment.

sk.overview: India's digital financial services and NBFC-led retail lending sector serves a large, young, credit-underpenetrated mass market. Formalization (GST, JAM/India Stack, eKYC), rising smartphone/internet penetration and low data costs are enabling tech-led NBFCs and fintechs to underwrite and serve borrowers that conventional banks have historically underserved, particularly in unsecured personal loans and loan-against-property.
sk.schemes: Digital India|JAM Trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) / India Stack|eKYC / DigiLocker|OCEN / ONDC|PMJDY financial inclusion|Udyam / MSME formalization
sk.structure: NBFCs hold ~18-19% of systemic credit and ~23% of the combined personal-loans and LAP market (FY2025), accounting for 25% of personal loans and 21% of LAP. Tech-led NBFCs/fintechs (Kissht, Moneyview, KreditBee, Fibe) capture share from cautious conventional lenders via digital-first, AI/ML …
